title: CLICK TO CALL CONGRESS: Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

sponsor.name: State of the People. Los Angeles Action Hub.

description:
# CALL CONGRESS: Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

## This is a national call to action.

Congress is advancing budget rollbacks that will directly harm Black communities — cutting healthcare, housing, food access, education equity, maternal health, and youth job training.

These are not policy tweaks. These are direct attacks on our futures.

**Sign up to take action. Then click to call. You'll get everything you need — including who to contact and what to say.**

---

## What Happens After You Sign Up

1. You’ll be directed to **call the U.S. Capitol Switchboard**  
   - **Phone Number:** (202) 224-3121  
   - Ask to speak to your **U.S. Representative** or **Senators** by name or ZIP code

2. You’ll get a **sample call script** (below)  
3. You’ll help stop harmful cuts — and demand what we’re owed

---

## Programs at Risk

- **Job Corps** – job access for Black youth  
- **Section 8 Housing Vouchers** – keeping families housed  
- **WIC & SNAP** – food access for mothers and children  
- **Medicaid** – healthcare for our elders, kids, and disabled neighbors  
- **Black Maternal Health Programs** – doulas, midwives, and prevention  
- **Community Violence Intervention (CVI)** – proven harm reduction strategies  
- **Public Schools (Title I)** – schools serving Black and low-income youth  
- **Pell Grants & Loan Forgiveness** – education access and debt justice  
- **Environmental Justice** – clean air, clean water, healthy communities

---

## Need to Look Up Your Rep?

- [Find your Representative – House.gov](https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative)  
- [Find your Senators – Senate.gov](https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm)

---

## Call Script

Hi, my name is [Your Name], and I live in [City], [ZIP].

I’m calling to demand that you vote NO on any federal budget that cuts funding for programs our communities depend on — including Job Corps, Medicaid, Section 8, SNAP, maternal health care, and community violence intervention.

These are essential services. Cutting them would cause real harm.

We demand equity, repair, and investment — not more harm.

Vote no on these cuts. Protect Black futures.


---

## Why It Matters

These budget proposals are part of a larger campaign to strip resources from our people, dismantle our safety nets, and erase our right to thrive.

But we are not silent. We organize.  
**Click to call. Speak your truth. Hold the line.**

Sign the form today and tell California legislators: **deliver floor votes for repair, redress, and Black futures.**

---

## What’s at Stake

- **SB 518** – *Establishes the California Reparations Bureau*  
  Creates a permanent state agency to coordinate and implement reparations-related programs for descendants of enslaved Black Americans.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB518)

- **SB 437** – *Creates Genealogical Standards for Eligibility*  
  Directs the California State University system to develop lineage-based standards to determine fair eligibility for reparations.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB437)

- **AB 57** – *Provides Homebuyer Assistance for Descendants*  
  Offers targeted homeownership support for descendants of enslaved Black Americans — a step toward housing justice and wealth repair.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB57)

---

## Why It Matters

California can set the national standard — but only if it chooses to act.

These bills aren’t about the past. They are about **repairing systemic harm**, restoring opportunity, and **building a future where Black communities are valued, resourced, and free.**

No more delay. No more symbolic gestures.  
**We need floor votes. We need action. We need repair.**

Pennsylvania voters, like voters in other states, strongly support these programs, and with good reason. Medicaid provides critical support for millions of Pennsylvanians.

The reconciliation bill will terminate healthcare coverage for around 13 million Americans and kick approximately 3 million Americans off of SNAP. While new requirements for the state to help pay for the SNAP program would result in new expenditures for the state of $226 million to over a billion. The bill does all this harm while adding $2.4 trillion to the federal deficit.

This event is open to everyone. Join Pennsylvanians Together and the Pennsylvania Policy Center, for a real conversation about proposals that could harm Pennsylvanians, and what we can do about them. title: Testimony Needed for EPA: Clean Air for Northwest Indiana
description:
On Wednesday, June 11th at 12:30 pm CT / 1:30 pm ET, you have the opportunity to tell your steel story directly to decision-makers in Indianapolis to help protect clean air and reduce pollution from coal-based steel production.  **On Wednesday, June 11th, at 12:30 p.m. CT / 1:30 p.m. ET,** you have the opportunity to speak directly with decision-makers in Indianapolis to help protect clean air and reduce pollution from coal-based steelmaking. 

Lake and Porter Counties are out of compliance with federal nitrogen oxide (NOx) pollution rules, and the state must submit a plan to the EPA to show how it will restore healthy air. **Currently, the plan does not require significant improvements at the steel plants despite their status as some of the largest NOx polluters in the county and state.** 

NOx pollution from steel mills and other heavy industries contributes to serious health problems like asthma, heart disease, and early death. Northwest Indiana has some of the dirtiest steel plants in the country, which utilize outdated technology that pollutes the air we breathe.  
IDEM’s plan doesn’t go far enough. It ignores cleaner, modern steelmaking methods that are already being used in other states and could improve public health, reduce pollution, and support good union jobs.

You can join the meeting virtually here or in person in Indianapolis. If you are interested in testifying in person, we can assist with arranging transportation. Please reach out to Mike Oles at [mike@mightyearth.org](mailto:mike@mightyearth.org) or 317-281-0568 to coordinate.

#### Exposing the Big ~BXXXXXiful~ UGLY Bill: Threats to US Economy & Democracy: Ed Spire, June 9@7 CST Zoom

_Ed Spire invites you to a critical presentation that will expose the profound dangers the “Big ~BXXXXiful~~ UGLY Bill” poses to both our economy and our democracy._

By dissecting the bill’s agenda, Ed will demonstrate how this sweeping legislation—marketed as a boon for working Americans—threatens to accelerate wealth inequality, undermine essential safety net programs, and erode the foundational principles of fair governance.

### RSVP here to let us know you will be attending -> https://mobilize.us/s/IZ6JBA

The bill’s central feature is trillions of dollars in tax cuts, overwhelmingly benefiting corporations and the ultra-wealthy, while slashing funding for healthcare, food assistance, and renewable energy. If enacted, the legislation would result in the largest transfer of wealth from working and middle-class families to the richest Americans in U.S. history, with households earning less than $51,000 losing an average of $700 per year, and the top 0.1% gaining nearly $400,000. 

#### These cuts are paid for by gutting Medicaid and SNAP, threatening healthcare coverage for over 8 million people and taking food assistance away from millions of children and families. Farmers, too, would be hit hard, with SNAP cuts risking $30 billion in lost income and 400,000 jobs.

Beyond the economic fallout, the bill’s provisions also threaten democratic norms by consolidating power among the wealthiest interests and stripping away programs that support broad participation in society. The rollback of clean energy incentives and the expansion of fossil fuel subsidies further entrench corporate influence over public policy, while new immigration fees and border measures risk marginalizing vulnerable communities. The bill’s rushed passage through the House, with no Democratic support and deep internal divisions, underscores the lack of broad democratic consensus.

_Join Ed Spire to learn what’s at stake, how these changes could reshape our nation for generations, and what you can do to help stop this unprecedented attack on economic fairness and democratic values._

Now is the time to raise your voice, contact your senators, and mobilize your community to demand a better, more just future for all.

title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum in Delphos
description:

## WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?

- Senate Bill 1  (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
- SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
- SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
- SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
- We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
- Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
- For more information, visit [ohiosb1petition.com](ohiosb1petition.com)
- Sign the petition to repeal SB1!
